lesson.title: Effects of the Cold War
lesson.summary: How the superpowers kept their influence through proxy wars, the arms race, and aid.
learningGoals: Compare the ways in which the United States and the Soviet Union sought to maintain influence over the world.
lesson.bigIdea: The superpowers avoided fighting each other directly but spread their rivalry around the world through proxy wars, nuclear weapons, and aid.
lesson.context: Nuclear weapons made a direct war between the superpowers unthinkable, so their competition took other forms.

sections.title: Proxy wars

blocks.text: Instead of fighting each other, the superpowers backed opposite sides in proxy wars, conflicts in which they armed and supported local forces. In Korea from 1950 to 1953, US-led United Nations forces fought North Korean and Chinese troops.

In Vietnam, the United States sent more than 500,000 troops to defend South Vietnam, but North Vietnam, supplied by the Soviet Union and China, won in 1975. In Angola, Cuban troops supported by the Soviet Union backed one side in a civil war, while the United States and South Africa backed another. In Afghanistan from 1979 to 1989, the United States armed guerrillas fighting Soviet troops.

blocks.title: Comparison
blocks.text: Both superpowers used military aid and advisers, but the United States sent large armies to Korea and Vietnam, while the Soviet Union sent its own army to Afghanistan.

sections.takeaway: Proxy wars brought superpower rivalry and great destruction to Asia, Africa, and Latin America.

sections.title: The arms race

blocks.text: The Soviet Union tested an atomic bomb in 1949, and both sides then built thousands of nuclear weapons. This arms race led to a balance based on mutually assured destruction: neither side would attack because both would be destroyed.

In 1962 the Cuban Missile Crisis brought the world close to nuclear war after the United States found Soviet missiles in Cuba. The Soviets removed the missiles after the United States promised not to invade Cuba. The rivalry also drove a space race, from Sputnik in 1957 to the Moon landing in 1969.

blocks.title: Cause and effect
blocks.text: Fear of nuclear war led both sides to avoid direct conflict and, after 1962, to sign the first arms control agreements.

sections.takeaway: Nuclear weapons made the superpowers rivals who could not afford to fight directly.

connections.title: Proxy wars and decolonization
connections.body: Many proxy wars were fought in newly independent states, linking the Cold War to decolonization.
connections.transferQuestion: Why did so many Cold War conflicts take place in former colonies?
connections.feedback: Explain how new states' weakness or divisions invited superpower involvement.
